text.p: - Russian troops, hastily withdrawn from Chechnya, have been left to survive in empty fields beyond the borders of the rebel republic with a minimum of supplies and no money.
- The murder of six Red Cross workers in Chechnya must have been perpetrated by those who stand to lose everything in the forthcoming presidential election in the separatist republic.

- Russian tourists willing to visit Britain often have to go through a protracted and humiliating chain of queueing, interviews and interrogations at the consulate in Moscow. Staff treat all applicants as liars and keep the obligatory $60 visa fee even when they turn down the application.
- The new suggested tax on crossing the Russian border infringes the constitution and international law.
- Russia faces an internal debt crisis if yields on state securities remain high while the economy posts no growth, says the paper, quoting a finance ministry official.
- Russian diamond producers may have to look for a new bulk buyer for their production as De Beers threatens to stop serving one of its biggest suppliers.
- A wave of terrorism sweeps through rebel Chechnya as tensions rise between the separatist republic and its neighbours.
- The speed of Boris Yeltsin's recovery fails to keep pace with the advertised schedule.
- There are still 1,187 Russian citizens being held in captivity in Chechnya.
- Two men died in a helicopter crash near Moscow on Tuesday.
